correctness.rationale: For odd m, a(m)=(sigma(m)-lambda(m))/4. If lambda=0, LTE forces a(m) odd precisely for one odd-exponent p=3(mod8) with exponent 1(mod4); if lambda is nonzero, local sigma-lambda modulo 8 separates a single p=5(mod8) with exponent 1(mod4), and the Jacobi (2/t) branch for m=t^2. The published dyadic formula flips parity exactly for squares and k>=2. Factorization m=p^(4h+1)u^2, prime number theorem for classes 3 and 5 modulo 8 and sum of reciprocal odd squares pi^2/8 give F(X)~pi^2 X/(16 log X), then summing k gives pi^2 X/(8 log X). The h>=1, p|u and square remainders are O(sqrt X); the sum tails are o(X/log X). Direct signed counts checked for 109 n, full exact formula and parity for first 200000 n via extracted package code. These checks supplement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: Signed two-block partitions form a naturally studied 2026 arithmetic coefficient sequence. Their complete parity support across odd prime exponents and all dyadic levels and the asymptotic frequency pi^2 X/(8 log X) settle the natural question of how frequently signed coefficients are odd. This supplies an exact global structural classification and a genuine prime-scale invariant; it is not a small arbitrary cutoff, isolated test or renamed OEIS A192717 sequence. No priority is claimed for the source coefficient formula or preexisting proper subfamily.
